# AgentLatch

> AgentLatch is an open-source, local-first AI agent security scanner. It checks Python agent code, agent manifests (tools, permissions, authentication), and prompt templates for risks such as prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, over-privileged tools, unauthenticated tool endpoints, code execution, unsafe deserialization, memory poisoning, agents that rewrite their own prompts or install persistence, and hardcoded secrets. Findings map to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications. It runs as a CLI (`agent-latch scan`), a pre-commit hook, or a GitHub Action, and outputs text, JSON, or SARIF. MIT licensed; early proof of concept.

Key facts:

- Install: `pipx install agentlatch-security` or `python -m pip install agentlatch-security` (Python 3.11+); add the `[runtime]` extra for the MCP proxy and `[audit]` for `--dependencies`. The PyPI package is `agentlatch-security` (it provides the `agent-latch` command); `agentlatch` on PyPI is an unrelated project.
- Containers: `ghcr.io/agentlatch/agent-latch` (scanner) and `ghcr.io/agentlatch/agent-latch-runtime` (MCP proxy), non-root, pinned dependencies, no Node.js.
- Scan: `agent-latch scan /path/to/agent`; audit a manifest with `--config agent-manifest.yaml`; fail CI with `--fail-on high`; a manifest is optional, and every folder and text file is scanned. Suppressions inside the scanned project (`.agent-latch-ignore`, inline ignore comments) apply only with `--project-ignores`.
- GitHub Action: `uses: AgentLatch/agent-latch@v0.5.1` (https://github.com/marketplace/actions/agentlatch-scan).
- Frameworks with specific checks: CrewAI, LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, smolagents, and common memory and vector-store clients. Generic rules apply to any Python code. JavaScript/TypeScript are not scanned.
- Privacy: scans run locally and never call an LLM. Only the opt-in `--dependencies` audit sends package names and versions to an advisory service.
- Runtime proxy (preview): `agent-latch-runtime proxy -- <MCP server command>` sits between an AI app and an MCP server and records tool lists, tool calls, results and prompts (argument names and hashes, secret-masked excerpts). `agent-latch-runtime import-logs` joins those logs into one event per message (printed, plus `events.csv` and `normalized.jsonl` under `runtime-logs/`) and runs the bundled gates: ALR04 flags instruction-like content in tool definitions, ALR05 flags it in tool results, and ALR10 flags secret-like values sent to a tool or returned in its output (it reads only masked payloads, so no raw secret is ever written). Results go to `gate-results.csv`. `--database FILE` also keeps those events in a local SQLite file; it is off unless set, and it does not upload them. `agent-latch-runtime demo` runs the whole flow against a bundled synthetic server (`--scenario poisoned-output` shows ALR05, `--scenario secret-leak` shows ALR10). Monitor only: it reports findings and never blocks a call. `agent-latch --runtime-result` prints every gate's findings from `runtime-logs/gate-results.csv` in the scan table, with a local tool's file and line when the project defines that function. The report lists findings only.
- Audit store (preview): `agent-latch-runtime import-logs --database FILE --anchor PATH` seals every stored event in a hash chain and publishes the newest seal; `agent-latch-runtime verify --database FILE --anchor PATH` reports intact, unanchored, tampered, deleted, rewritten or missing; a store that fails its check is refused (exit 1). Detects tampering; keeping the store in another OS user or container prevents it. Docs: docs/ledger.md.
- Tamper-evident audit ledger (preview): `agent-latch-runtime proxy --ledger trace.ledger.jsonl` seals every trace record into a local SHA-256 hash chain; `agent-latch-runtime anchor --ledger … --to /mnt/audit/anchors.jsonl` publishes one short digest where the agent cannot write, and `agent-latch-runtime verify --ledger … [--trace …] [--anchor …]` returns `intact`, `unanchored`, `tampered`, `deleted`, `rewritten` or `missing`. `agent-latch --runtime-result --ledger … --anchor …` prints that verdict in bold above the findings (grouped by gate), and a failed trail exits 1 even with `--fail-on none`. The runtime event store (`import-logs --database`) is sealed and append-only the same way: `verify --database` and `agent-latch --runtime-result --database … [--database-anchor …]` report its verdict, and a store that does not seal its rows is ALR15-R02. Standard library only, local, never in the request path; the gate is ALR15 (ASI10).
- Limits: the scanner uses static heuristics; there is no runtime enforcement or model-behavior testing. A clean scan is not a security guarantee. The audit ledger proves a log was not changed after recording, not that what it recorded was safe; without an anchor it cannot catch a full rebuild.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/README.md): overview, install and how-to sections (scan, CI, runtime, ledger, connect an app), FAQ
- [Getting started](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): install, command reference, output formats, exit codes, ignoring false positives
- [Agent manifests](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/agent-manifest.md): `agent-manifest.yaml` format and the checks it enables
- [pre-commit and CI](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/ci.md): pre-commit hook, GitHub Action inputs and outputs, other CI systems
- [Detection rules](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/RULES.md): every rule, its OWASP mapping, and known blind spots
- [Gates](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/GATES.md): security outcomes (`ALR01`–`ALR15`); every rule and runtime check belongs to one gate, reported as `PY001 (ALR06)`
- [Audit ledger](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/ledger.md): making the runtime log tamper-evident — hash chain, anchors, the six verdicts, limits; then [setup](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/ledger-setup.md), [reference](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/ledger-reference.md), [operations](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/ledger-operations.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/docker.md): scanner and runtime images, `docker run -i` for MCP apps, limits, verifying an image; then [setup](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/docker-setup.md)
- [Runtime proxy (preview)](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/blob/main/docs/runtime.md): install, connecting an MCP client, what is recorded, limits

## Examples

- [Vulnerable agent demo](https://github.com/AgentLatch/agent-latch/tree/main/examples/vulnerable-agent): a deliberately insecure project and the findings it produces
- [Demo video](https://youtu.be/4FrRWlApDpo): scanning the vulnerable example and failing CI with `--fail-on high`
